text:
incident-bot: PAGED 2345678901 - streaming: spike in SSE disconnects + tool-call parse failures in prod-us-west-2. Pager -> @alex

alex: acknowledged. I'll take lead. Paging SRE + runtime. Attaching root query for logs -> https://logs.redwood.internal/streaming?query=parse_error%20tool_call

jamie: looking at ingest nodes, first anomalies around 2345678840. lots of connection resets followed by parse errors. pulling correlation ids now.

maya: added context: we shipped a parser refactor at 2345677000 that changed tolerant-json default to false. flag may be the regression.

ryan: several customers reported truncated function outputs then client reconnect loops. Support case #5482 from tenant "AcmeAnalytics" noting degraded runs.

chris: confirm. Our batch jobs saw ~30% of sessions fallback to non-streaming. Happened intermittently across jobs starting ~2345678850.

alex: quick timeline: deploy 2345677000 -> first errors 2345678840 -> pager 2345678901. Jamie, paste sample logs / correlation ids you grabbed.

jamie: sample from ingest-3:
```
2026-03-15T12:07:21.843Z ERROR streaming/parser.go:142 parse_toolcall: json.Unmarshal failed: invalid character '\\n' in string literal
correlation_id=cf2a1b7f
session_id=ses-9a3f
client_ip=54.12.34.56
```

maya: that matches the tolerant-json toggle. Parser now expects complete JSON per chunk; some older clients split top-level function call payloads across SSE events and send trailing newlines. Previously we concatenated and tolerated newlines, new behavior fails on chunk boundaries.

ryan: client behavior caused retries and reconnect loops, amplifying visible impact. One customer lost ~20% throughput in that window.

alex: mitigation choices (fast): 1) rollback deploy 2) flip tolerant-json flag on via config 3) force non-streaming route for affected tenants. Pro/cons?

maya: flipping tolerant-json=true is a 5-minute config change via manager and safe. Rollback is heavier and risks other unrelated fixes. Server-side reassembly would be ideal but needs dev time.

jamie: I'll prepare a kubectl patch to toggle env var and do a canary first. Command I'll use:
```
kubectl -n streaming patch deployment streaming-parser --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/1/value","value":"true"}]' --context=prod-us-west-2
```
Will do rolling restart after patch.

alex: do it. Also create temporary routing rule for affected tenants to force non-streaming if we see failures during patch.

jamie: applied to canary at 2345679140. Can confirm logs show tolerant mode enabled:
```
2026-03-15T12:19:03.112Z INFO streaming/parser.go:98 tolerant mode enabled
correlation_id=cf2a1b7f
```

alex: roll to 50% then 100% and monitor.

jamie: 50% at 2345679227, 100% at 2345679251. parse error counts dropped to zero in the window for us-west-2.

ryan: drafted customer advisory: "Temporary mitigation applied, monitoring. Full RCA coming." Liz, can you coordinate tenant comms and account teams?

liz: yes. Need tenant ids and timings. ETA 30m to push advisory to affected accounts. I'll add mitigation timestamps and next steps.

chris: can confirm streams recovered for our runs after ~2345679300. Thanks.

maya: preliminary root cause hypothesis: PR #5123 changed parser behavior (tolerant-json=false). Clients that split tool-call JSON across SSE frames produce incomplete chunks that cause json.Unmarshal to fail. Regression introduced by parser refactor.

jamie: supporting evidence: error correlation by client SDK version shows concentration in older SDKs. Query used:
```
index=stream-logs parse_error=1 | stats count by client_sdk_version
```
Result: sdk_v1.2.0 -> 189 errors, sdk_v1.3.1 -> 7 errors.

alex: impact assessment: three enterprise tenants in us-west-2 experienced ~15-30% session degradation during 2345678840-2345679300. No data loss or exfiltration. Availability/UX impact only. No SLA breach raised yet but we will include in postmortem.

liz: customer notes to include: impacted window, mitigation timestamps, temporary tolerant mode, plan for permanent fix, contact for follow-ups. I'll own outbound comms and will post advisory to account teams by EOD.

maya: RCA action items (in-thread):
- Confirm PR #5123 is the regression and create revert candidate or feature-flag change
- Add integration/unit tests that simulate SSE-frame-splitting of function call payloads
- Backfill and scan logs across regions for similar errors or toggles
- Implement server-side reassembly to allow strict parsing while tolerating frame splits (target: 48h)

alex: owners: maya -> runtime patch + tests, jamie -> rollout verification + log collection, liz -> customer comms, ryan -> support follow-ups.

alex: does anyone object to leaving tolerant-json=true as a temporary safety valve while we build the proper fix? We should weigh risk of older tolerant behavior vs customer outages.

maya: no objections. We'll treat tolerant mode as short-term mitigation and prioritize reassembly implementation.

jamie: I'll increase parse-error alerting sensitivity for 24h and post follow-up in #incidents.

ryan: support will contact the three affected accounts and attach the mitigation summary.

chris: thanks for the quick patch. Keep us posted on permanent fix timeline.

alex: artifacts and logs for RCA: logs-export id logs-export-2345679305, timeline doc https://docs.redwood/internal/incident/2345678901/timeline, PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/5123. We'll convert this thread into formal RCA and link artifacts.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE 2345679350 - mitigation applied, severity downgraded to P2. Follow-ups scheduled for owners.

---
Notes for post-incident RCA doc: include exact queries, correlation ids list, canary rollout timestamps, customer impact numbers per tenant, PR diff excerpts, and the test coverage plan.
